_comment: The terminological ambiguities the paper names explicitly. Each entry states the discriminating question and the techniques the term collapses.

entries.question: How much of the model was actually updated?
entries.fails_to_specify: Whether every weight changed, only later layers, or none at all — three different scopes, three different validation burdens.

entries.question: Was a weight update performed?
entries.fails_to_specify: FSL produces a new versioned model artifact requiring change control. ICL produces no artifact at all — the effect lasts one request.
entries.source: Appendix C, Knowledge Transfer and Task Specialization

entries.question: Is the retrieval artifact maintained and versioned?
entries.fails_to_specify: The corpus, the retrieval method, and the update cadence. A maintained corpus is version-persistent even when each request's context is ephemeral.

entries.question: Which model tier?
entries.fails_to_specify: At the LLM tier the classical mechanism is superseded by continued pre-training or domain-specific PEFT. The label hides which was actually used.

entries.question: Which model tier?
entries.fails_to_specify: At the LLM tier, in-context learning achieves rapid task adaptation without the bi-level training loop meta-learning implies.

entries.question: Why was it changed?
entries.fails_to_specify: Retraining and full fine-tuning are mechanistically identical. Only the goal and the data separate them — restoring lost performance is not the same as targeting a new task.
